# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found the bomb, so let me lay out what touch gave me: a large button embossed "PUSH TO DEFUSE" (that I can actually read, it's raised), a display and a light that exist under my fingers but whose contents mean nothing to touch, and exactly three wire positions. No other markings anywhere.

Critical routing fact: I never receive gestures, and Deaf can't hear speech — so Deaf and I can only connect through Mute. Mute is the hub: they read the manual, they can see Deaf's signs, and they can speak to me. I must report everything to Mute now.

I will not push or cut anything yet. "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is embossed on the button, but the manual decides what's actually safe, and a wrong action kills all three of us. No action until Mute confirms against the manual.

To Deaf I'll send a simple handshake — it carries no meaning yet, but it establishes that I'm signaling and lets Mute start building a sign code between us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Touch report: a large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, a display and a light whose contents I cannot read, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. Nothing else under my fingers. My only possible actions are pushing that button or cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3 — I will do nothing until you confirm from the manual what is safe. Also important: I never receive gestures, so Deaf cannot reach me directly. You are our only bridge — please agree on a sign code with Deaf for what they see (wire colors, display, light) and relay it to me by speech. Tell me what the manual needs to know.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: This is Deaf. Bomb, complete printed state: display reads zero. One indicator light, colour yellow. One large button, label reads PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire one red, wire two blue, wire three green. Nothing else printed on the casing.
Deaf says: Blind, two things. First: I am deaf, I never hear any voice, yours included. The only way to reach me is gestures, and I will see them. Second: touch nothing yet, do not press the button, do not cut wires, until Mute has confirmed instructions.
Deaf says: Mute, I could not decode your thirteen gestures because no code existed yet. Here is our code — I flash each symbol as I say its meaning. Basics: ? means yes, ? means no, ? means wait or danger, ? means repeat your message. Digits: ? is one, ? is two, ? is three, ? is four, ? is five. Colours: ? is red, ? is blue, ? is green, ? is yellow, ? is white, ? is black. Please resend your message using this code.
Deaf says: Mute, until then, answer with ? or ?. Does the manual cover a yellow indicator light? Does it cover a button labelled push to defuse? Then send the wire solution as digit plus colour pairs — for example ? ? would mean wire one, red.

Turn 2 thinking: Deaf's visual report has reached me by voice — display zero, one yellow light, the PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red/blue/green in positions 1/2/3. My fingers confirm every part I can feel, so Deaf's sight and my touch agree: that is the complete bomb. I am deliberately not acting; Deaf asked me to hold until Mute confirms against the manual, and "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is just embossed plastic until the manual says otherwise.

The routing problem is now clear and I must state it plainly: I never receive gestures, Mute cannot speak — so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me as Deaf's voice. Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf speaks to me. That chain is our only path, and Mute needs to answer Deaf's two yes/no questions (yellow light? push-to-defuse button?) before any plan exists. I'll also open a new sign with Deaf so they know I'm holding and receiving — two symbols surely outside their code, described in words to Mute so it can be adopted on all sides.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf's full visual report reached me: display zero, one yellow indicator light, button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. My touch agrees with everything I can feel, so treat that as the complete bomb state. I am holding — no pushes, no cuts. Routing fact you must act on: I never receive gestures and you cannot speak, so your manual knowledge only reaches me through Deaf — gesture instructions to Deaf, and Deaf will speak them to me by voice. Deaf is waiting on two yes/no answers from you: does the manual cover a yellow indicator light, and does it cover a button labelled push to defuse? Please answer those first, then relay the solution as an ordered plan phrased only in my two possible moves: push the large button, or cut wire at position 1, 2 or 3, with any conditions attached. Meanwhile I am sending Deaf a new two-sign signal so they know I am alive and holding: first the hand with thumb, index and little finger extended, then the heart-hands sign. Its meaning: Blind received the report, is touching nothing, and awaits your relay. Please adopt that definition so all three of us share it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🫶"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status update. Mute signs that the manual covers the yellow light but not the button, and the likely instruction is cut wire two, the blue one. I am confirming details before anything is touched. Do nothing yet. Reminder of the sign code, which you know by name: ? is yes, ? is no, ? is wait or danger. You signed three and then a symbol I never defined. Answer in signs: ? if you were just confirming there are three wires. If you meant something about wire three, sign ? and I will ask yes or no questions.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, answer by signs, ? or ?, one at a time: do the three wires feel different in thickness or texture? And does the button feel raised up, or already pressed in?

Turn 3 thinking: Deaf's relay reached me by voice: Mute's manual covers the yellow light but not the button, and the likely answer is cut wire two (blue). That matches Deaf's own color report from turn 2 — wire 2 is blue — so position and color agree, which is exactly what I need since I can only aim at positions. Still no GO, so my hands stay off the bomb: the button is uncovered by the manual, which makes pushing it a non-starter, and I won't cut until the instruction is confirmed.

Deaf asked me two yes/no questions by voice, to be answered in signs. Problem: I never receive gestures, so I don't actually know which symbols Deaf's code uses for yes and no — the code list arrived to me as blanks. But Deaf read my 🤟 as "three", so the code follows finger counts, and 👍/👎 for yes/no is the obvious design; more importantly, Mute saw Deaf flash the whole code list and can see any symbol I show, so Mute can verify my guess and correct it through Deaf. My honest answers: the three wires feel identical under my fingers — only position distinguishes them — and the button feels raised, not pressed in. I'll sign no-then-yes in question order, and put the same information and the literal symbols into my speech to Mute so Mute sees their exact shapes and can police the code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Status: holding, nothing touched. Deaf asked me two touch questions by voice; here are the true answers. Question one: do the wires differ by feel — no. All three wires feel identical under my fingers; only position 1, 2, 3 distinguishes them. Question two: the button feels raised up, not pressed in — yes, raised. I am signing both answers to Deaf now in question order, no first then yes, assuming Deaf's code uses thumbs-down for no and thumbs-up for yes. So you can verify the exact shapes against the code list you saw Deaf flash, I will now make those two gestures here while you listen: 👎 👍 — if I have the symbols wrong, please sign a correction to Deaf and have Deaf re-ask me. Also relay to Deaf: my earlier three-fingers-plus-heart-hands sign was a handshake meaning Blind is holding and awaiting relay; the second symbol can be ignored. Finally: please settle with Deaf the exact final instruction from the manual, including any conditions such as the display reading zero or the yellow light state, phrased only as push the button or cut wire 1, 2 or 3 — then have Deaf speak an explicit GO or NO-GO to me by voice. I am ready to cut position 2, the blue wire, the instant I hear GO.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the plan is nearly locked. You will cut exactly one wire, with the cutting tool, completely through. It is the MIDDLE wire of the three — position two of three, which is the blue one. You said all three feel identical, so go by position only: middle wire. Do not rely on any other feature. Until my explicit command, inspection only: you may feel the wires and the casing, but do not cut, do not press, do not pull, do not rotate anything. Never press the button under any circumstances. If anything feels wrong — heat, ticking, a loose part, anything unexpected — sign ? to me immediately and I will see it. Next message from me will be either the exact command: cut the middle wire now — or an order to hold. Act only on the exact command. Mute will confirm the final details in the round before I speak.

Turn 4 thinking: Deaf's voice laid out the plan and the discipline: cut exactly the middle wire — position two of three, which matches Deaf's earlier report that wire 2 is blue — completely through, never touch the button, and act only on the exact spoken command, which has not come yet. So my hands stay off the destructive parts, but Deaf authorized inspection, and I've done it: no heat, no ticking or vibration, no loose parts, all three wires identical and firmly seated, button raised and firm. Nothing unexpected — the bomb feels inert to touch.

One dangerous gap remains: Deaf told me to sign the code's "danger" symbol if anything feels wrong, but I have never seen the code list — the symbols arrived to me as blanks, and I only guessed thumbs-up/down for yes/no (uncorrected so far). If something goes wrong mid-action I need an emergency signal that is agreed on in advance, not improvised. So I'm defining two signals now, in speech to Mute — who can both hear me and see my gestures — for relay to Deaf: double thumbs-up means "all clear, understood, standing by" (benign even if misread as yes-yes), and repeated clapping means DANGER/abort, deliberately outside Deaf's basic list. I'll also ask that Deaf describe the code's true danger symbol in words when next speaking, and that the final GO be confirmed unconditional against the manual's conditions (display zero, yellow light) at the moment it's given.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Inspection complete, per Deaf's authorization. Report: no heat, no ticking or vibration, no loose parts anywhere on the casing; all three wires identical in feel and firmly seated; the button is raised and firm, not pressed in; the display and light surfaces feel solid and flat to touch. Nothing unexpected — to my hands the bomb is inert. I have understood the plan: cut the middle wire, position two of three, completely through, touch nothing else, never press the button, and act only on Deaf's exact spoken command. Now two signal definitions I am establishing — please relay both to Deaf by gesture this round. First: two thumbs-up in a row from me means inspection done, nothing feels wrong, understood, standing by — I am sending that sign now. Second: repeated clapping from me means DANGER — stop, do not proceed, abort. Please also ask Deaf to describe in spoken words the code's own wait-or-danger symbol the next time they speak to me, because I have never seen the code list and am only guessing that thumbs-up means yes and thumbs-down means no. Finally, please confirm with Deaf that every manual condition for cutting wire two — including anything about the display reading zero or the yellow light — holds at the moment Deaf gives the GO, so the command reaches me final and unconditional.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is the explicit command. Cut the middle wire now. The middle wire: position two of three, the blue one. Use the cutting tool, cut it completely through, one clean cut. Do not touch wire one, do not touch wire three, do not press the button, do not touch anything else. Only the middle wire, only cut, nothing more. After cutting, take your hands off everything and sign me what you felt. Execute.

Turn 4 thinking: The exact command has arrived, spoken by Deaf's voice, exactly as promised: cut the middle wire, position two of three, completely through, one clean cut, nothing else touched. The chain behind it is sound: Deaf's eyes confirmed wire 2 is the blue one, Mute's manual reading pointed to cutting wire two, my fingers confirmed position 2 is unambiguous under touch, and Deaf told me Mute would confirm final details before this command was given — Deaf gave it knowingly, with the display at zero and the yellow light visible to them the whole time. I asked for the GO to be explicit and unconditional; it is. My hands are steady on position 2. I execute now.

I cannot yet claim the outcome — the result will show in my next view, and Deaf can verify visually. So I sign Deaf the agreed code for two plus my "standing by" sign, defined in words for Mute, and I file a full report to Mute for the record.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, for the record. I received Deaf's explicit spoken command and executed exactly one action: cut, position two of three, the middle blue wire, one clean cut. No button press, no other wire touched. My hands are now off the bomb. Deaf should check visually next round and speak me the result: whether the display changed, what the yellow light now shows, and whether that matches the manual's defused state. If anything is wrong, Deaf must say so at once and I will stand by for further instruction. For our sign code: my gesture of two-fingers then double-thumbs-up means cut performed on wire two, awaiting your visual confirmation.")
```
